newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil wants role in Nordic power market.
newsitem.headline: Statoil wants role in Nordic power market.

text.p: Norwegian state oil company Den Norske Stats Oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday it was positioning itself to become a Nordic energy company.

"That will give us a role in a future regional electricity market," Gunnar Myrvang, Statoil Senior Vice President for natural gas business development, was quoted as saying by the company's Status Weekly newsletter.

Statoil owns a one-third stake in Naturkraft, which is planning to build two 350 megawatt gas-fired power stations on the west coast of the country. The plants, if approved by parliament, will be the first gas-fed units in Norway, which relies exclusively on hydroelectricity for its own production or on imports from Denmark and Sweden.

"Norway is currently failing to meet its power needs from domestic sources. Without developing new hydro or gas-fired electricity capacity, the country must expand imports from Sweden and Denmark," Status Weekly said.

Norway and Sweden already run a single power market with a joint trading exchange. Finland is expected to join its two neighbours next year, while Danish participation will require more time due to domestic legislation.
Statoil said current growth trends indicated that Denmark, Finland, Norway and Sweden needed to expand annual electricity output by three-seven terawatt hours every year for the next decade.
"Norwegian natural gas could become a new energy source in the Nordic power market," it said.
